findings.title: Duplicate containers-auth probe creates parallel maintenance owners
findings.why_it_matters: Changes to the containers-auth lifecycle contract now require editing two byte-identical runtime probes, so a correction to permissions, preservation, or dry-run coverage can leave the other platform testing an older contract. The Linux and Darwin suites exercise distinct delivery boundaries and should remain independent, but their shared probe implementation need not be copied. Extracting the probe preserves both executions while giving the assertions one maintenance owner.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the identical authEffects Python body into tests/lib/containers-auth-effects.py and reference that file from both Nix checks. Retain the Linux activation block and Darwin materialized step extraction, and continue running both platform suites.
evidence: Read and compared both complete authEffects definitions: their 37-line Nix blocks are byte-identical, including the fresh-home, dry-run, exact JSON, file/directory mode, and existing-byte preservation assertions.

tests/darwin-outputs.nix:220-221 extracts stepBlock containersAuth from the materialized generation and executes authEffects; tests/podman-containers.nix:239 executes the same probe over authBlock. These callers preserve distinct platform delivery coverage when the probe is shared.

testing_gaps: Matching-platform execution was unavailable for the Linux owner checks and the tailscale-provisioning KVM mutation case. The new CI mutation venue must establish baseline success, intended builder diagnostics, and restored controls before those proof repairs have runtime evidence. This review inspected code and consolidation structure; it did not execute host or VM builds.
